title: Your First Weekend at Illinois Institute of Technology, Shared as Cards
description: A Friday-to-Sunday introduction to Illinois Tech through its student center, Modernist campus, recreation spaces, Bronzeville history, lakefront, and nearby public landscapes.

cards.title: Start Beneath the Exelon Tube
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Find the campus crossroads
cards.notes: Begin at MTCC, locate student services and dining, then use the overhead Green Line tube as an unmistakable campus landmark.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop inside Illinois Tech’s distinctive student center.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Tech identifies MTCC as its student center and says it contains dining, student-group offices, WIIT-FM, a post office, and other services beneath the Exelon Tube.
cards.access_notes: Campus-center access and individual service hours may vary; confirm posted building and dining schedules before entering.

cards.title: Read the Clear-Span Landmark
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Architecture from the public approach
cards.notes: Walk south along State Street and study the raised entry, black steel frame, and uninterrupted upper floor from the exterior.
cards.short_summary: A close look at the Mies-designed home of Illinois Tech architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Tech states that S. R. Crown Hall is a National Historic Landmark, has a clear-span design without internal support beams, and houses the College of Architecture.
cards.access_notes: The exterior can anchor the stop; do not assume studio or interior access without checking university building access.

cards.title: Set Up Your Library Base
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Learn where help and equipment live
cards.notes: Find the upper-level Research Help Desk and note where to return for subject help, computer access, or a circulating laptop.
cards.short_summary: An early orientation to the main library’s people, tools, and study support.
cards.evidence_claim: Galvin Library’s official pages place the Research Help Desk on the upper level and document computer workstations and first-come, first-served circulating laptops.
cards.source_title: Need Help? | Paul V. Galvin Library
cards.access_notes: Consult the library’s live schedule before visiting; weekend, break, and ID-controlled access can differ.

cards.title: Follow the Campus History Markers
cards.subtitle: Saturday late morning · Read Bronzeville history in place
cards.notes: Use the university booklet to locate the seven markers, pausing at Mecca Flats, Binga Bank, and Alpha Suffrage Club sites.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided route connecting the campus landscape to earlier Bronzeville places.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Tech’s Black Metropolis booklet documents seven campus cultural markers, including markers for Mecca Flats, Binga Bank and Arcade, and the Alpha Suffrage Club.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor self-guided route; follow the booklet’s map and remain on normal campus walkways.

cards.title: Try a Drop-In Recreation Option
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Move between orientation stops
cards.notes: Bring your student ID and ask what is available before choosing open gym, open swimming, fitness space, or a scheduled class.
cards.short_summary: A flexible active break centered on Illinois Tech’s recreation facility.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Tech says every student has access to Keating for its facilities, fitness classes, intramural leagues, and tournaments; the catalog also lists open swimming and open gym.
cards.access_notes: Student eligibility does not establish current availability; verify facility schedules, entry requirements, and equipment rules first.

cards.title: Meet the Lake at 31st Street
cards.subtitle: Saturday late afternoon · Campus-to-lakefront outing
cards.notes: Walk or take transit east for skyline views, then stay on open paths and observe posted beach and water-safety notices.
cards.short_summary: A nearby lakefront pause with skyline, harbor, and accessible recreation features.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chicago Park District identifies Margaret T. Burroughs Beach as 31st Street Beach and documents skyline views, restrooms, concessions, an accessible playground, and a public fishing dock.
cards.access_notes: Swimming is seasonal and subject to posted conditions; consult current Park District notices and use designated areas only.

cards.title: Take a Sunday Tree Walk
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · See Mies Campus as a living collection
cards.notes: Cross campus slowly, compare labeled woody plants where available, and photograph how the tree canopy frames Modernist buildings.
cards.short_summary: A public, no-admission walk through Illinois Tech’s accredited arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Tech states that the 120-acre Alphawood Arboretum contains more than 1,800 plant specimens and is free to visit and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The arboretum spans the outdoor Mies Campus; use public paths and respect any temporary campus restrictions.

cards.title: Learn the Campus Disc-Golf Layout
cards.subtitle: Sunday late morning · Informal outdoor recreation
cards.notes: Locate the course before playing, bring discs or confirm borrowing options separately, and yield to pedestrians on shared grounds.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor game that turns the campus landscape into a navigable course.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Tech’s current catalog explicitly documents a disc golf course on campus and presents it as an informal recreation option.
cards.access_notes: The source does not establish equipment availability, course condition, or event conflicts; check locally before starting play.

cards.entity_name: Ed Kaplan Family Institute for Innovation and Tech Entrepreneurship
cards.title: Trace the Innovation Hub’s Purpose
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Connect the building to hands-on work
cards.notes: View the Kaplan Institute exterior, then note how its maker spaces, media labs, and collaborative areas support project work.
cards.short_summary: A visual introduction to the university’s cross-disciplinary innovation hub.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Tech describes the Kaplan Institute as an innovation hub containing workshops, media labs, classrooms, collaborative hubs, emerging technologies, and maker spaces.
cards.access_notes: Use the exterior as the dependable stop; interior rooms, workshops, and equipment may require authorization or scheduled access.

cards.title: Finish Beside the Chicago River
cards.subtitle: Sunday late afternoon · A public-landscape finale in Chinatown
cards.notes: Explore the paved paths and elevated boardwalk, watch for wetland and prairie habitat, and leave wildlife undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: A riverfront conclusion with accessible paths and native habitat.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chicago Park District says Ping Tom Natural Area has more than three acres of prairie and wetland habitat, paved paths, an accessible overlook, and daily 6 a.m.–10 p.m. hours.
cards.access_notes: Open 6 a.m.–10 p.m. daily according to the current Park District page; follow posted natural-area rules.

warnings: The sequence is evergreen rather than event-specific; verify live library, recreation, dining, building, transit, and seasonal beach conditions before departure.
Coordinates and maps URLs are null because they were not independently verified from the cited direct evidence pages.
The historical-marker route is marked free because the university documents outdoor campus markers intended for visitors; it does not require admission or a purchase.
